To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the LKM antibodies, which are found in some patients with chronic active hepatitis, react with a protein in the liver-kidney-microsomal fraction of rats.

(i) LKM antibodies were identified in sera from patients with HBs antigen negative chronic active hepatitis, and were not detected in sera from patients suffering from other liver diseases or from other diseases, including autoimmune diseases; (ii) these antibodies react with a microsomal antigen present in liver and kidney; and (iii) the antigen was localized to a density of 20 g/ml in CsCl gradient fractions, and was destroyed after treatment by trypsin and by chymotrysin

LKM antibodies can be detected in patients with chronic active hepatitis by a radioimmunoassays, that these antibodies are not detected in other diseases, that they react with a protein antigen of 58 kDa that is localized in the microsomes of rat liver, kidney and stomach, that this antigen is not solubilized by detergents, and that it is destroyed by proteases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new type of autoimmunity in chronic hepatitis, which is characterized by LKM antibodies, and is not associated with other autoantibodies.
the detection of LKM autoantibodies and their relationship to other autoantibodies in patients with chronic active hepatitis.
the detection of a new type of autoantibodies directed against an antigen present in the endoplasmic reticulum of liver and kidney.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LKM antibodies represent the serological counterpart to the cytoplasmic autoantigen of the liver and the proximal renal tubule, and are associated with a distinct subgroup of CAH.
LKM antibodies represent a specific marker in the diagnosis of CAH, but that the antigen is not restricted to liver and kidney.
the LKM antigen is a cytoplasm membrane component which is not solubilized by detergents, is resistant to RNA and DNA degradation, but sensitive to trypsin and/or chymotryp-sin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the LKM antibodies are a new autoantibody system, which can be distinguished from other autoantibodies in liver disease by RIA.
LKM antibodies are directed to an antigen which is located in the endoplasmatic reticulum of liver and kidney cells.
we have developed a radioimmunoassays for detection of LKM antibodies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can now detect the presence of the LKM antibody in a patient’s blood.
we have developed a new method for detecting liver-kidney autoantibodies that can be used to diagnose a specific subgroup of chronic liver diseases.
the LKM antibodies are not a marker of PBC, but rather of a distinct subset of HBsAg-negative chronic active hepatitis.
